note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for multidisciplinary treatment planning following recent PSA rise and prior prostate cancer diagnosis.

Recently relocated 70-year-old graphic designer, widowed and currently residing with his sister. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms, consistent with an IPSS of 19, and uses a walking frame due to mobility limitations. He exercises with light weight-training twice weekly and consumes approximately 5 units of alcohol per week. Recent ophthalmology review for cataracts was unremarkable. His PSA has fluctuated over recent years, rising from 1.7 ng/mL in June 2024 to 2.5 ng/mL in January 2025. He has no active medication allergies and takes no regular medications. His medical history is significant for a prior TURP.
Per rectum, a discrete nodule is palpable in the right basal peripheral zone, consistent with clinical stage cT2a. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs and no lymphadenopathy.

admin: Mobility limitation (frame); ground-floor consult room preferred.
